newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa shares hug weak prices but close off lows.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa shares hug weak prices but close off lows.

text.p: South African shares established their fate by noon and stood by it -- finishing frail but off the day's most sickly levels.
Dealers said the underlying trend remained weak and the market was unlikely to stage a robust recovery on Wednesday.
Bashed from the start by futures players cashing in on reverse arbitrage -- selling stock and buying futures -- shares fell steadily and by noon had established the prices they intended to cling to.

The firmer rand was seen offering some support on Wednesday, but dealers said underlying sentiment was weak and the market was more likely to shun a slightly stronger rand and rather be spooked by prevailing interest rate hike worries.

October CPI due at 0900 GMT on Wednesday had already been more or less discounted by the market and while trade might back off a tad ahead of the data's release, the number was unlikely to hold any surprises, dealers said.
They said trade had been pretty mixed with both locals and foreigners active in reverse arbitrage.
Wall Street -- expected to open lower -- was not seen giving much direction as dealers said the local market had ignored the U.S. trend for a while now.
Industrials lost 48.9 points to finish at 8,086.9, dragging the all-share 49.3 points lower to 6,866.
Golds were still hindered by the depressed bullion price and unassisted by a firmer rand. Dealers did not expect the gold board to shine unless bullion climbed above $380 again.
Gold shares hugged their weaker levels to finish 24.2 points lower at 1,687.2.
